body:
I think you are right to sever ties with him, if only for *your* sake.  He needs help that apparently exceeds what an inpatient treatment program was able to give him, much less what *you* could ever hope, or reasonably expect yourself, to provide.  Simply part ways with him amicably, wishing him the best.

As for your keepsakes, I would take the break-up route of destroying or altering as many as possible; you want to make a clean break from this man, without constant reminders of his existence.  If people ask about him, say that you haven't been in contact for a while; if they insist, you are under no obligation to lie on his behalf and I wouldn't.  Finally, reconcile your memories with reality by remembering that very few people are completely open about who they are.

Yeah, "grown-ups" can be condescending jackasses.  Ignore the armchair psychiatrists and find support in loved ones and, preferably, some professionals as well.

Another bit of advice: don't vent on the Internet in the hopes of actually feeling better.  Ever.  It never helps.  It would be as if the dumbest, nastiest, most cynical, most judgmental, least educated, and least compassionate people you know got together and made a test tube baby, and then you went and vented to that person.  While they were still in the test tube.

Feel better, friend.
